limitations: One calendar-selected week per month, not annual averages or random sampling
Calendar service-day mix is controlled; dispatch decisions and PV profiles can differ
Fixed 2026 timetable templates evaluated on 2025 dates; not historical 2025 bus operations
Historical estimated actual irradiance and training-only 2024 climatology; not Solcast forecast skill

No reuse of old four-season outputs as results of this twelve-week campaign

A day-ahead diagnosis is neither a completed week nor a monthly comparison; no completion email is sent.
1% certificates refer to Stage 1 relaxation and fixed-assignment Stage 2 separately; no integrated global optimality claim.
The valid lower bound can improve without reducing the incumbent cost; report those improvements separately.
Native soft memory termination is not optimality. Root completion requires an optimal MIPNODE event; a zero-node MIP callback alone is insufficient.
Endpoint recurrence adds continuous equality states without imposing a new upper bound. Reduced matrix size alone is not evidence of objective improvement, physical acceptance or optimality.
No extra BESS reserve or inventory restoration. Empty means the retained 20% physical SOC floor, full means the 80% ceiling; it does not mean a zero-kWh battery.
Only the currently issued block retains protection of the physical floor against unobserved PV. No initial-inventory reserve is protected.
Initial BESS energy may be consumed: report initial/final inventory and net change separately. Lower cost under this policy is not evidence that a solver found a better solution to the old policy.
Existing fixed-command controller is retained. BESS discharge/charge commands must be physically feasible before execution; excessive commands remain errors, not hidden post-solve repairs.
The earlier dense-model NoRel run hit the memory limit before improvement. Lower memory with endpoint support motivates this bounded test but does not prove NoRel will fit or improve cost.
Prior NoRel reached 24.0967 GB peak despite an 18 GB soft limit and failed route-band validation. A soft limit is not a hard peak-memory bound; report measured memory honestly.

A prior barrier attempt used dense charging support and 12 threads and stopped before the root LP. This endpoint/4-thread test is not a re-labeling of that run. Root completion and cost improvement are uncertain, and even root completion may leave the 1% target unmet.

Disabling crossover requires barrier for both root and node relaxations; numerical accuracy and search speed may differ. Physical tolerances are unchanged. Root completion does not prove the declared 1% target or integrated total-cost optimality.
First-incumbent fixed-assignment Stage2 total has not been saved. Stage1 incumbent improvement is not an initial-to-final total-cost saving.
